title: Sherpa Tensing — Descent Seven: Future Simple Passive (B1)
description: The tense of promises and notices about the future — and in the passive, of promises with nobody attached to them. You will be contacted. By whom…

hero.lede: The tense of promises and notices about the future — and in the passive, of promises with nobody attached to them. You will be contacted. By whom, exactly? The sentence has been built so that you cannot ask.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the future simple with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The work will be carried out by a specialist firm."

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

cards.head: With the doer
cards.ex: "It will be handled by the duty team."

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes will be + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: They will close the road overnight.
The road will be closed overnight.
A specialist firm will carry out the work.
The work will be carried out by a specialist firm.
The firm stayed, at the end.
They will lose two hundred jobs.
Two hundred jobs will be lost.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Nothing changes for the subject at all. Will be is the same for everybody, exactly as at camp seven, and the participle sits behind it.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: After be comes the participle. Close here is an adjective meaning near.
The be is not optional; it is what makes the sentence passive.
You will be contacted by we.
You will be contacted by us.
After by comes an object pronoun: us, him, them.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows:
The thing it happens to.
"The road will be closed."

The one who does it.
"They will close the road."
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: Almost every official notice about the future is written this way, and it is worth noticing what that buys the writer. Staffing levels will be reviewed commits nobody to reviewing them. We will review staffing levels does. Same future, one accountable sentence and one that is not.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.label: Interactive
sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The event — now the subject
items: You will be contacted within five days.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … and nobody at all is losing them.

quiz.explain: Will be + the participle. Will close would say the road closes itself.
Will be is the same for every subject, and the participle follows.
Will be contacted. Note the total absence of anyone who will do the contacting.

quiz.prompt: The work _____ by a specialist firm. (carry out)
quiz.explain: The phrasal verb keeps its particle, and the doer goes behind by.
By takes an object pronoun: us, not we.
Lose / lost / lost. Notice that nobody is doing the losing.
Last year is a finished past time, so the past simple passive.
Will be reviewed. The active version would name whoever has to do it.
Will be told, with the participle of tell.
Will be sent. Send / sent / sent.

quiz.prompt: Nothing _____ before the report is finished. (decide)
quiz.explain: Nothing is the subject and it is not deciding anything, so the passive.
Will be answered — with, as ever, nobody named as the answerer.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
